claims.text: Reportable infections: certain infectious diseases (eg, COVID-19, HIV, syphilis, tuberculosis) must be reported to state or local public health agencies.
claims.quote: certain infectious diseases (eg, COVID-19, HIV, syphilis, tuberculosis) must be reported to state or local public health agencies.

claims.text: Abuse and neglect: signs of child abuse and, in many states, adult or elder abuse or neglect typically must be reported to protective services.
claims.quote: Signs of child abuse and, in many states, adult or elder abuse or neglect, typically must be reported to protective services.

claims.text: Driving: in some states, conditions that might seriously impair a patient’s ability to drive, such as dementia or recent seizures, must be reported to the Department of Motor Vehicles.
claims.quote: In some states, conditions that might seriously impair a patient’s ability to drive, such as dementia or recent seizures, must be reported to the Department of Motor Vehicles.

claims.text: Child abuse: physicians and other professionals in contact with children (including physician assistants) are mandated reporters, required by law in every state to report suspected child abuse or neglect.
claims.quote: physicians and other professionals in contact with children (eg, nurses, physician assistants, nurse practitioners, social workers, psychologists, teachers, day care workers, police) are mandated reporters who are required by law in every state to report incidents of suspected child abuse or neglect
claims.locator: Management: Reporting to the appropriate agency

claims.text: Suspicion is enough: it is often unclear after the first evaluation whether abuse occurred; the mandatory report of suspected abuse brings in the authorities or social agencies to investigate.
claims.quote: Often it is unclear after the initial evaluation whether abuse occurred. However, the mandatory reporting requirement of suspected abuse should engage appropriate authorities and/or social agencies to investigate

claims.text: Liability: a report made on reasonable cause and in good faith is immune from criminal and/or civil liability, while a mandated reporter who fails to report can be subject to criminal and civil penalties.
claims.quote: Any person who makes a report of abuse based on reasonable cause and in good faith is immune from criminal and/or civil liability. On the other hand, a mandated reporter who fails to make a report can be subject to criminal and civil penalties.
claims.locator: Management: Reporting to the appropriate agency

claims.text: Where to report: Child Protective Services in the United States, or another regionally appropriate child protection agency.
claims.quote: The reports are made to Child Protective Services (if in the United States) or another regionally appropriate child protection agency.
claims.locator: Management: Reporting to the appropriate agency
